radiusSource: Radius 1.30 +/- 0.01 Jupiter radii, temperature 770 +/- 75 K and mass 3.75 +/- 0.5 Jupiter masses: the evolutionary-model row (Saumon & Marley 2008 hybrid clouds, 24 +/- 3 Myr) of Balmer et al. (2025, arXiv:2411.05917), Table 4: 92,939.6 km at 71,492 km per Jupiter radius. Their atmosphere fits give radii from 0.5 to 1.8 Jupiter radii and temperatures from 760 to 1260 K, the 'radius problem' of their section 5, so the evolutionary values are used. A sphere: no oblateness is measured.
orbitalPeriodSource: Derived: Kepler's third law with the sample's semi-major axis 8.898 au and total mass 1.2955 solar masses, 23.3 years of 365.25 d. Balmer et al. (2025, arXiv:2411.05917): the orvara fit to VLTI/GRAVITY, SPHERE, NIRC2 and NaCo astrometry with the Hipparcos-Gaia accelerations, distributed as a posterior of 1,000 samples by whereistheplanet 1.0.1 (post_aflepb.hdf5), which stores no likelihoods. Smallest chi-squared against the three GRAVITY positions (20.6).

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius in the shared neutral gray. No image, colour, map or oblateness of AF Lep b is measured; only its size, mass and orbit are.

effectiveTemperatureSource: 770 +/- 75 K, the evolutionary-model row of Balmer et al. (2025), Table 4, https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.05917
semiMajorAxisSource: The recorded orbit's semi-major axis, 8.9 au at the sample's parallax, from the posterior of Balmer et al. (2025, arXiv:2411.05917) (packages/astronomy/data/bodies/af-lep-b.json). Franson et al. (2023) found 8.4 +1.1/-1.3 au.
massSource: Dynamical mass 3.75 +/- 0.5 Jupiter masses, Balmer et al. (2025, arXiv:2411.05917), Abstract.
